newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African vigilantes miss surrender deadline.
newsitem.headline: S.African vigilantes miss surrender deadline.

text.p: Two leaders of a South African Moslem vigilante group failed on Thursday to meet a police deadline to turn themselves in on charges of organising an illegal protest at Cape Town international airport, police said.
Police spokesman John Sterrenberg said the leaders of People Against Gangsterism and Drugs (Pagad), Aslam Toefy and Abdus- Salaam Ebrahim, had missed the 3 p.m. (1300 GMT) deadline.
"There is a warrant out for their arrest, but we told them they could volunteer to come forward. They have not done so," Sterrenberg said.
The warrant was issued on Wednesday after Pagad tried on Monday to demonstrate at Cape Town airport, which the group said was being used to smuggle in drugs.
Police said the demonstration was illegal and fired tear gas and rubber bullets, arresting a total of 24 vigilantes during the demonstration and a later protest outside a police station.

President Nelson Mandela warned Pagad ealier this month it had overstepped the mark in its campaign against gang leaders and told vigilantes they would not be allowed to demonstrate at airports or other sites where tourists would be affected.
Pagad leapt to prominence in August when members killed the leader of a notorious gang before television news cameras.

Mandela's government initially showed some sympathy for the group's anti-crime programme but police officers said this week PAGAD's actions put it in the same category as the gangs it claimed to be fighting.
The 24 PAGAD members arrested on Monday are due to appear in court on Friday to apply for bail.
